sample_unit: patients with advanced HIV disease screened with dCXR/CAD
models_evaluated: computer-aided detection (CAD) software for chest X-ray, nationally adopted threshold ≥0.5

links.outcome: CAD sensitivity and specificity at the nationally adopted threshold in the local advanced HIV population
links.effect: At the ≥0.5 threshold, sensitivity was 50% (58/116; 95% CI 41–59), specificity 92%, PPV 85%, NPV 65.9%. Half of TB cases were missed; threshold optimization for this population is recommended.
links.quote: However, at the adopted threshold of ≥0.5, CAD demonstrated high specificity but low sensitivity (50%) in this population, missing half of all TB cases.

links.outcome: TB diagnosis rate among patients with normal CAD result (false reassurance from negative screens)
links.effect: TB was diagnosed in 30% (43/143) of patients with a normal CAD result, 52% (15/27) of abnormal non-suggestive, and 85% (58/68) of suggestive cases; NPV was 65.9%.
links.quote: TB diagnosis rates increased sharply with CAD score: 30% (43/143) in normal, 52% (15/27) in abnormal non-suggestive, and 85% (58/68) in suggestive cases.

unlisted_practices: Using CAD as a confirmatory decision-support tool rather than a standalone screening test in advanced HIV disease
Population-specific optimization of the CAD score threshold

screen.reason: Evaluates the real-world clinical implementation of digital chest X-ray CAD for TB screening in advanced HIV disease patients, assessing the operational performance of the nationally adopted threshold (>=0.5).
